items.followUp: Describe how an enzyme and its substrate interact according to the induced-fit model.

rubric.why: Shows that the substrate’s shape fits the enzyme’s active site.
rubric.description: The substrate fits the specifically shaped active site, like a key fitting a lock.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the specific fit between the substrate and active site.

rubric.why: Identifies the enzyme-substrate complex and what happens after binding.
rubric.description: An enzyme-substrate complex forms; products leave, and the enzyme remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complex and either the products leaving or the enzyme remaining unchanged.

modelAnswer: The substrate has a shape that fits the enzyme’s active site, like a key fits a lock.
An enzyme-substrate complex forms; the reaction produces products, which leave the enzyme unchanged.

items.followUp: Compare arteries, veins and capillaries in terms of their walls and the direction or role of blood flow.

rubric.why: Describes the artery’s wall and the direction in which blood flows.
rubric.description: Arteries have thick, elastic walls and carry blood away from the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a thick artery wall and blood flow away from the heart.

rubric.why: Gives distinguishing features and the direction of blood flow in veins.
rubric.description: Veins have thinner walls, contain valves, and carry blood towards the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct vein wall or valve feature together with blood flow towards the heart.

rubric.why: States the characteristic thickness of capillary walls.
rubric.description: Capillaries have walls only one cell thick.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that capillary walls are one cell thick.

rubric.why: Explains the role of capillaries in exchange between blood and tissues.
rubric.description: Capillaries allow materials to be exchanged between the blood and body tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing exchange of materials between blood and tissues.

modelAnswer: Arteries have thick, elastic walls and carry blood away from the heart.
Veins have thinner walls, contain valves, and carry blood towards the heart.
Capillaries have walls only one cell thick.
This thin wall allows exchange of materials between the blood and body tissues.
